comment: Online-service redirects for PSPC (src/runtime/hle/modules/net_infra.cpp, docs/pspc-network.md). Same format as PPSSPP's infra-dns.json: per game, the disc IDs it covers, 'domains' (host name -> address of a revival server) and/or 'dns' (a revival DNS server that answers for all of the game's names). 'tunnel' (optional) names a public server that is reached over HTTPS only (a Cloudflare Tunnel carries nothing else): PSPC starts a relay for the game (server/pspc_gamespy/relay.py) that listens at 127.77.0.1, where 'domains' then send the game. An infrastructure.json next to pspc.exe takes precedence over this file: its entry for a game replaces this one, so a server on this PC (the launcher's Online page) overrides the public one. 'hosts' lists the servers each game was seen to use, for revival server authors; it isn't used for redirecting.

games.name: Syphon Filter: Combat Ops
hosts: combatops.psp.online.scea.com:10071 (SCE-RT Medius lobby, TCP; resolved by the game's own DNS queries)

games.name: Star Wars Super Squadron
hosts: The same GameSpy names and ports as Elite Squadron (below), all at the public server swss.pspc.online (docs/gamespy-server.md, 'Public server'). Behind a Cloudflare Tunnel instead of forwarded ports, the entry has "tunnel": "https://swss.pspc.online" and "domains": {"*.gamespy.com": "127.77.0.1"}

games.name: Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron
hosts: A server for all of them: server/pspc_gamespy (docs/gamespy-server.md); redirect *.gamespy.com
